# mmf-mage.3 — a Gnome Mage, one life shorter: what a crow costs, and what a spell list really is

*Seed 1, Gnome Mage, build `e473720ed88a`. Carried on from `mmf-mage.2` (which
carried on from `mmf-mage`). 54 answers, 1061 keypresses, turn 8019. **Died on
depth 2, killed by a crow**, with 8 of 8 hit points and **11 experience — one
short of the 12 a Gnome needs for CL2**. Gold 7, AC 17, 23 flasks of oil, 4
Cure Light Wounds, 2 Scrolls of Phase Door, 2 Wooden Torches, a Book of Magic
Spells, one Robe, one pair of Leather Gloves and one unknown Yellow Potion
left in the pack. Character level 1. Deepest level of this life: 2 (the
lineage's deepest is 3, from `mmf-mage`).*

## 1. What happened

The character came to me on depth 1 with 8 of 8 hit points, 2 of 2 spell
points, AC 17, 24 flasks of oil and 7 gold, standing in a room that had been
sealed since the life before mine. The plan I wrote down was: *descend to
depth 2, where a kill pays double, and spend the spell points on the first
cast of a spell, which pays experience.* The plan worked, mostly. The
character died.

* **Asks 145-151 — reading the level.** The level's known area is a dead-end
  tree. The room I inherited (level x 8-23, y 30-46) is walled all round;
  its only opening is a one-tile notch in its east wall at level x 24, and
  the only other door in it, at level x 18, y 40, is a **closet**: the tile
  west of it is wall. The corridor east of the room runs to the vertical
  corridor, which ends at the up staircase in the north and in a long
  east-west corridor in the south. Nothing in the known area leads anywhere
  except into the dark.
* **Asks 152-160 — the first kill.** A detection cast (the one my past life
  made) had left two down staircases known at level (23,21) and (66,12) and a
  third found later at (91,63). The room east of the room held two monsters:
  a **white worm mass** (10 hp, AC 1, 2 experience) and a **large white
  snake** (11 hp, AC 36, 2 experience). One flask of oil killed the worm mass
  (AC 1, so about 89 per cent to hit), and the sidebar's NXT went from 10 to
  8 — which is also how I know my past life's report was wrong: it said the
  character had 0 experience, but the Gnome's CL2 threshold is 12 (the
  character sheet says `Adv Exp 12`), so the character I inherited already had
  **2** experience from its first Find Traps cast.
* **Asks 161-168 — the potion.** The two `!` items in the room were both
  **unknown Yellow Potions**. I drank one: it was a **Potion of Neutralize
  Poison**, whose kind is level 5, so its first use paid **5 experience** — the
  best single decision of the run, one third of what CL2 needs. The second
  potion I kept: with Neutralize Poison out of the pool its expected value
  falls to about half an experience against a 15 per cent chance of Sleep,
  Blindness, Confusion or Poison, and Blindness would have cost me the map I
  was navigating by.
* **Asks 169-186 — the staircase.** The third down staircase was 30 tiles east
  and 9 south. A digit string of twenty-four `6` walked me twenty-three tiles
  along a straight corridor in **one** ask; ten steps south along a
  one-wide passage put me on the staircase. Along the way a **giant white
  mouse** (2 hp, AC 4, 1 experience) died to one flask. On the staircase I
  rested: `R`, backspace, `*`, Enter filled the spell bar from 0/2 to 2/2 in
  one ask, and the rest was not interrupted.
* **Asks 187-191 — depth 2.** `> ` took me down. The level is fresh: the
  detection spell found its doors and its down staircase at level (94,12), and
  I stood on its up staircase at level (132,30) with 1 spell point and 1
  experience short of CL2. Then I aimed the game's own walk eight tiles east,
  and the walk stepped into a **crow**.
* **Asks 191-199 — the death.** The crow (depth 2, 9 hp, AC 14, 8
  experience, **sleepiness 0 — it never sleeps** — two bites of 1d3 at **speed
  120, so it attacks twice a turn**) killed an 8-hit-point mage. The character
  sheet at the death screen reads `HP -2/8`, `Cur Exp 11`, `Adv Exp 12`. The
  remaining asks were spent in the death menu: I answered `n` to two quit
  prompts and pressed Escape once, which in Angband is the quit command, and
  twelve `6` keys sent while a prompt was open had already opened the
  character sheet, the equipment list and that quit menu.

## 2. The decisions I would take back

1. **I aimed the game's walk into a monster I had not looked at.** The
   aimed walk (`*`, `p`, digits, `g`) computes its path with unknown ground
   treated as passable and then *steps onto whatever is there*. The walk moved
   one tile and the crow was on the second. One `l` (look) or one `[` (the
   monster list) before the walk would have shown it. **The game's own walk is
   the fastest way across the dark and the most dangerous one, and a monster
   on depth 2 that never sleeps is a death sentence for 8 hit points.**
2. **I did not take the depth-2 level seriously enough as a new danger.**
   Depth 1's monsters were AC 1 to 4 and asleep; depth 2 has sleep-0 monsters
   (the crow, the wild cat) and armoured ones, and my character had 8 hit
   points, 0 spell points and no idea what was around the arrival point. The
   manual's rule — *gate each descent on the worst round of the depth you are
   entering* — says a depth-2 soldier does 14 in a round, and the crow does
   up to 12 in a turn at speed 120. **A CL1 mage with 8 hit points should
   arrive on a new level with a full spell bar, not 1.**
3. **Six asks went into the spell list before I understood it, and four more
   into the quit menu.** The spell list's rows are the spells I have
   **learned**; the screen prints every spell in the book with `unknown` or
   `difficult` beside the ones I cannot use. A letter selects by *index into
   the menu's rows*, so every letter I pressed cast the one spell I knew.
   **You cannot cast a spell you have not studied** — which also means the
   +4 experience of a first Magic Missile was out of reach at CL1, because my
   one spell slot already held Find Traps.
4. **I spent 22 asks walking to a staircase on depth 1 and the level's known
   area was a dead-end tree all the same.** A fresh depth-1 level would have
   cost the same 22 asks and given a different map. **The level that is
   behind you is worth nothing; the only thing that matters is whether the
   next level has a staircase you can walk to.**
5. **I did not drink the second Yellow Potion, and I was right not to — but
   for the wrong reason.** I kept it because its expected value had fallen to
   half an experience. The right reason is that the potion's value is in its
   kind's level, and the kinds worth points are Neutralize Poison (5) and
   Poison (3, and it hurts you). **Drinking an unknown potion for experience
   is a bet on the pool, not on the potion.**

## 3. Where the manual was wrong, or not enough

* **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §9's Mage block says a mage "Learns one spell at
  CL1 (G, book, spell)".** True, and the consequence is not in the manual: at
  CL1 my only slot held Find Traps, so **the first-cast experience of Magic
  Missile and Light Room (4 each) was unreachable until CL2**. The manual
  lists the first-cast experience (four, four, two, four, four) as if it were
  a fixed sum, without saying that a slot is what buys it.
* **The manual says "`b` browse, `G` study" and nothing about what the cast
  list does.** The game's own cast list prints all seven of the Mage's spells
  with their failure chances, but it only *has* the ones you have learned.
  Nothing in the manual or in the strategy manual says the letters on that
  screen label the rows you can pick.
* **The manual's "one command per ask" rule is right but does not cover a
  prompt that is already open.** A `-more-` takes **one key per page** and
  the message line goes *back* to the first page, so the number of keys to
  clear a message is not visible on the screen. And the whole-level map ends
  with `Hit any key to continue`, so an answer after `M` loses its first key
  unless it starts with a space.
* **The manual never says that a digit string sent into a prompt can open
  menus.** Twelve `6` keys, sent while the game was in a prompt, opened the
  character sheet, then the equipment list, then the quit menu — and `n` in
  that menu is **New Game**.
* **The strategy manual's "notes for the borg" assume the program can read the
  game's variables.** A text player cannot see a monster's sleep state, and
  that is exactly what decides the fight: the crow's `sleepiness:0` means it
  is awake when you meet it, and the wild cat's `sleepiness:0` means the
  same. **Two of the depth-2 monsters that pay 8 experience each are never
  asleep.**

## 4. What I could not see, or could not do

* **I could not see the crow.** It was in the dark east of the depth-2
  arrival point, and my torch shows a 3x3 patch. The level's monsters are
  spread over the floor at about one per hundred and fifty squares, so
  meeting one is a question of how much floor I walk over, not of luck.
* **I could not tell a door from a closet.** Three of the four doors I found
  on this level were in walls I could not see past: the door at level (18,40)
  had wall on its west side, and the room I was locked in had a door at
  (18,40) whose only floor neighbour was the corridor. A door is a room
  entrance; it is also sometimes nothing at all.
* **I could not cast what I wanted.** Six asks went into the cast list
  because the screen shows spells that cannot be picked, and I read the
  screen instead of the source. The ask header does say where the menu's
  cursor is (`cursor at 15,4`), and that one line would have told me the
  cursor was on the row I already knew.
* **I could not use the experience I had earned.** The character died with 11
  experience, one short of CL2, and the potion that would have made the
  difference (a second Neutralize Poison, worth 5) was never drawn.

## 5. Leads

1. **A depth-2 crow can kill a CL1 Gnome Mage in one turn, and it never
   sleeps.** *Evidence:* the crow's row in `lib/gamedata/monster.txt` —
   `speed:120`, `sleepiness:0`, `blow:BITE:HURT:1d3` twice — and the death
   screen (`HP -2/8`). *How to test it:* one run that walks onto depth 2 and
   deliberately finds a crow, with the hit points and the number of crow
   turns it took, and one that does the same against a **wild cat** (also
   `sleepiness:0`, AC 14, speed 120, two claw/bite blows) to see whether the
   two are equally bad, and against a **white harpy** (speed 110,
   `sleepiness:10`) to see whether a sleeping monster is worth anything.
2. **The spell list's rows are the learned spells; the screen prints the
   whole book.** *Evidence:* the list at ask 162 printed seven rows with
   `unknown` and `difficult` beside them, but pressing `b` and then `2` and
   Enter cast Find Traps (row 2) again and again, and the header said
   `cursor at 15,4` — the fourth screen row, which is Find Traps. *How to
   test it:* one run that studies a second spell at CL2 and casts it, which
   also tests whether the +4 experience of a first cast of a studied spell
   really is paid (the source says `player_exp_gain(player, e * spell->slevel)`
   on the first *working* cast, `src/player-spell.c:527`).
3. **The first use of an unknown potion is worth its kind's level, and at
   depth 1 the pool's best kind is worth five.** *Evidence:* the Yellow
   Potion was a Potion of Neutralize Poison (`level:5` in `object.txt`) and
   paid 5 experience in one ask (NXT 8 → 3). *How to test it:* a run that
   drinks every unknown potion it finds, on a fresh level, and reports the
   kinds it drew against the pool's weights (Neutralize Poison 60, Speed 40,
   Heroism 40, Boldness 40, Cure Light Wounds 80, and the bad five at 10
   each).
4. **A rest is one decision for two spell points, and a rest is the only way
   to make a spell affordable.** *Evidence:* `R`, backspace, `*`, Enter on the
   down staircase at ask 182 filled the bar 0/2 → 2/2 and was not interrupted,
   while the spell points regenerate at about one per 71 actions while
   walking (`player_regen_mana()`: `msp × 197 + 524` in 65536ths per action). *How
   to test it:* one run that measures the rest's length in game turns on a
   swept corridor against one beside a sleeping monster, because the
   interruption cost is what decides where a mage can rest.
5. **The detection spell is the only way to find the rooms of a level, and the
   rooms are where the monsters are.** *Evidence:* the Find Traps cast on
   depth 2 found seven doors and the down staircase in two asks; the room on
   depth 1 held two monsters and the corridors I walked held none. *How to
   test it:* a run that counts monsters per room visited against monsters per
   corridor tile swept, with the doors marked from a cast, and which reports
   whether the doors the spell finds are the room entrances or mostly
   closets — on the level I died on, one of the four doors had no floor on
   the far side at all.
6. **A level's known area can be a dead-end tree, and then the only way on is
   a fresh level.** *Evidence:* on depth 1 every known tile led back to the
   room I started in; the way out was a one-tile notch in its east wall and
   then 23 tiles of dark. *How to test it:* one run that, at the start of a
   level, counts the known doorways and asks whether any of them leads to
   ground the character has not seen — the answer decides whether to spend
   the level's budget on walking or on rerolling it.
